doc: Injection-technique facts from the guide, paraphrased (no text copied): injection_points = the "Number" column of Tables I-II; sites = the Table "Site" cell; scan_start = where the guide starts the dynamic scan; manoeuvre = positioning / passive movement the guide uses to identify the muscle; at_risk = neurovascular structures the guide says to avoid. Technique notes: the guide recommends IZ-targeted injection with the "seeding" technique (its ref 7: Kaymak 2024, Can J Neurol Sci), e.g. two biceps IZ points reached through one lateral-to-medial puncture with a long (>= 5 cm) needle, and soleus compartments the same way (p.443). Per-muscle scan videos are in the guide's supplementary material.

technique_refs.citation: Kaymak B, Kara M, Abdulsalam AJ, Ricci V, Özçakar L. Optimizing botulinum toxin injections by minding the muscle architecture and its innervation zone: the "seeding" technique. Can J Neurol Sci 2024;25:1-3 (as cited by the guide, ref 7).

subscapularis.scan_start: start at the caudal tip of the scapula in the horizontal plane, move cranially past teres major and infraspinatus; only part of the muscle is visible (scapular shadow)

pectoralis_major.scan_start: cranial sternum in long axis, then lateral to the clavicular part

pectoralis_minor.sites: mid-portion of superior and inferior parts: 1 each
pectoralis_minor.scan_start: horizontal plane over the coracoid, move caudally past coracobrachialis; deep to pectoralis major

latissimus_dorsi.sites: mid-point of each of three lines: 1 each
latissimus_dorsi.scan_start: caudal end of the scapula in short axis, move caudally
latissimus_dorsi.at_risk: thin muscle close to intercostal muscles and pleura

teres_major.sites: not in Table I (text: midpoint inferior angle - posterior axillary fold)
teres_major.scan_start: caudal tip of the scapula, horizontal plane; first muscle appearing cranially

biceps_brachii.scan_start: just distal to the bicipital groove where the long-head tendon passes under the pectoralis major tendon, scan caudally
biceps_brachii.at_risk: lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve between biceps and brachialis

brachialis.at_risk: median nerve and brachial artery medially

brachioradialis.scan_start: lateral to brachialis at the elbow; BR, ECRL, ECRB superficial to deep
brachioradialis.at_risk: superficial branch of radial nerve between BR and ECRB

triceps_brachii.sites: lateral head 50%, long head 60%, medial head 60%: 1 each
triceps_brachii.scan_start: start at the humeral articular surface; long head becomes muscle last

pronator_teres.scan_start: start at the humeral articular surface
pronator_teres.at_risk: median nerve and brachial artery between brachialis and pronator teres

pronator_quadratus.scan_start: distal approach between radius and ulna
pronator_quadratus.at_risk: superficial radial nerve and radial artery superficial to the target

flexor_carpi_radialis.scan_start: proximal forearm; PT, FCR, PL lateral to medial

flexor_carpi_ulnaris.at_risk: ulnar nerve between FCU, FDP and FDS

flexor_digitorum_superficialis.scan_start: from the humeral articular surface, scan caudally
flexor_digitorum_superficialis.at_risk: median nerve, ulnar artery and ulnar nerve in the FDS/FDP septum

flexor_digitorum_profundus.scan_start: deepest muscle wrapping the ulna, move distally/medially

flexor_pollicis_longus.scan_start: distal approach; tendon to muscle between median nerve and FCR tendon
flexor_pollicis_longus.at_risk: superficial radial nerve and radial artery

extensor_carpi_ulnaris.scan_start: most proximal dorsal forearm in short axis (anconeus between humerus and ulna), move distally

abductor_pollicis_brevis.scan_start: transducer perpendicular to the long axis of the thumb

opponens_pollicis.scan_start: deep and medial to APB toward the thumb

adductor_pollicis.scan_start: thenar scan; transverse head deep to deep head of FPB

lumbricals_hand.scan_start: ulnar to adductor pollicis along the 2nd metacarpal

palmar_interossei.scan_start: dorsal hand, slide from 1st to 5th metacarpal

dorsal_interossei_hand.sites: 75% (palmar and dorsal together: 7); 1st dorsal interosseous: 1 at mid-muscle
dorsal_interossei_hand.scan_start: dorsal hand, slide from 1st to 5th metacarpal

psoas_major.scan_start: posterior approach: posterior superior iliac spine in short axis, iliac crest and gluteus medius

piriformis.scan_start: posterior superior iliac spine in short axis; long axis by tilting the lateral transducer edge caudally
piriformis.manoeuvre: passive knee flexion with hip internal/external rotation shows piriformis moving under gluteus maximus
piriformis.at_risk: sciatic nerve (may pass under, through or above the muscle)

sartorius.scan_start: axial over the medial femoral condyle, move proximally

adductor_longus.scan_start: distal third of medial thigh (adductor canal), move proximally

adductor_brevis.scan_start: from the 30% level, between adductor longus and magnus

adductor_magnus.scan_start: axial over the adductor canal at mid-femur

gracilis.scan_start: supine, axial over the medial femoral condyle, slide proximally

semitendinosus.scan_start: axial over the posterior medial femoral condyle (ST superficial, SM deep tendons)

biceps_femoris.scan_start: axial over the posterior lateral femoral condyle
biceps_femoris.at_risk: sciatic nerve shifts under biceps femoris proximally

rectus_femoris.scan_start: axial over the quadriceps tendon, slide proximally

vastus_lateralis.scan_start: as rectus femoris; may not fit one image

gastrocnemius.scan_start: axial on the posteromedial popliteal fossa for the medial head

soleus.sites: posterior part 35% and 45%, anterior part 45%, medial and lateral: 2 each
soleus.scan_start: most distal posterior leg in short axis (tibia, FHL, Kager fat pad, Achilles tendon), move proximally

flexor_digitorum_longus.scan_start: axial behind the medial malleolus (FDL tendon posterior to TP tendon), move proximally

flexor_hallucis_longus.scan_start: short axis over the medial malleolus
flexor_hallucis_longus.manoeuvre: passive flexion/extension of the great toe identifies FHL
flexor_hallucis_longus.at_risk: muscle-belly apex in close contact with the tibial nerve

tibialis_anterior.scan_start: axial between fibular head and tibia on the anterior leg, scan distally
tibialis_anterior.at_risk: anterior tibial artery and deep peroneal nerve beneath EDL

extensor_digitorum_longus.at_risk: anterior tibial artery and deep peroneal nerve beneath EDL

extensor_hallucis_longus.manoeuvre: passive movement of the great toe identifies it
extensor_hallucis_longus.at_risk: anterior tibial artery and deep peroneal nerve beneath EHL

fibularis_longus.scan_start: from the lateral malleolus (distal) or the fibular head (proximal)

flexor_digitorum_brevis.scan_start: axial over the calcaneus, move toward the toes; beneath the plantar fascia

flexor_hallucis_brevis.scan_start: axial on the plantar 1st metatarsal head, move proximally (heads from the sesamoids)
